architectureDecisions: I introduces a read-only CausalReconstruction service; it resolves canonical stores/artifacts but receives no write-capable acceptance, claim, dispatch, recovery or policy-publisher ports.

CausalObservationSubject explicitly pins project/product history/projection and acceptance-currentness identities for historical queries; current queries first resolve those canonical heads then pin the subject.
Current blockers and remaining work derive from ProductStateProjection + exact current CrossDomainObligation/OrganizationWorkContract/lifecycle refs; observer input cannot provide a subset.

Execution identity is reconstructed from immutable ExecutionAttemptBinding and RuntimeExecutionAttestation: policyRef, strategyRef, contextRefs, toolsetRef, modelProfileRef, harnessRef, runtime deployment, semantic attempt id and runtime invocation id.

Accepted semantic/product/quality facts are explained by following immutable refs through completion/publication/lineage/release/snapshot/observation/acceptance/history/outcome artifacts; every output fact carries evidenceRefs.

Lifecycle timing uses a separate immutable CausalLifecycleEvidence artifact emitted by the owning production boundary at materialized/actionable, claim/release, runtime start/finish and publication/acceptance transitions. It is observational evidence only and cannot gate authority.

Existing RuntimeExecutionAttestation.startedAt/finishedAt are reused as runtime timing truth. Missing earlier lifecycle timestamps are never backfilled; the observer returns MISSING_PROVENANCE for unavailable waiting segments.

Waiting duration is defined from the durable actionable/materialized boundary to first runtime start for the same work generation; executing duration is the sum of persisted runtime invocation intervals for the pinned semantic attempt. Recovery intervals remain separately visible.
Observation projections are content-addressed/disposable. Deleting them and rebuilding from the same pinned subject yields identical facts/evidence identities; newer heads require a new subject.

Observation can report uncertainty/missing provenance but cannot turn it into acceptance findings or remediation commands. Integration J may consume I evidence later through a separate authority boundary.
implementationSlices: I1 — Observational provenance [AC-6, INV-2, INV-6, INV-7]: add immutable CausalLifecycleEvidence and a write-only evidence sink invoked by owning boundaries at real transitions. Reuse runtime attestation timestamps; never backfill missing historical time.

I2 — Pinned observation subject [AC-8, AC-9, INV-4, INV-8]: define CausalObservationSubject from exact product/projection/acceptance/history heads plus optional historical refs; current query resolves then pins, historical query never silently advances.

I3 — Blocker/owner/lineage reconstruction [AC-1, AC-2, AC-3, INV-4, INV-5]: traverse complete projection, obligations, work contracts, claim/currentness and derivation edges to explain blocker, remaining owner and invalidation chain without routing decisions.

I4 — Execution identity/timing [AC-4, AC-5, AC-6, INV-3, INV-6]: resolve exact attempt binding + runtime attestations, expose pinned HOW/config identities, calculate durable waiting/executing intervals, and emit MISSING_PROVENANCE when any required boundary is absent.
I5 — Evidence chain [AC-7]: follow exact completion/publication/lineage/deployment/snapshot/runtime-observation/quality/history/outcome refs and attach evidenceRefs to every accepted fact.

I6 — Read-only observer + fresh-process proof [AC-8, AC-9, AC-10, INV-1, INV-7, INV-8]: expose query-only OrganizationObserver, persist no authority state, rebuild deterministically in a fresh process and run B-H regressions.
